record.paper_title: A List of Problems on the Reverse Mathematics of Ramsey Theory on the Rado Graph and on Infinite, Finitely Branching Trees
record.original_question: How do the reverse-mathematical strengths of the rainbow Ramsey theorem for the Rado graph compare when the colorings are of different finite graphs; are the strengths all the same, or does the number of vertices in the finite graph being colored affect the strength?

evidence.quote: How do the strengths of the rainbow Ramsey theorem for the Rado graph compare for colorings of different finite graphs?
Are they all the same, or does the number of vertices in the finite graph being colored affect the strength?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Rado graph $\mathcal{R}$ is the unique (up to isomorphism) countable graph satisfying the extension property: for every pair of disjoint finite sets of vertices $U,V$, there exists a vertex adjacent to every vertex of $U$ and to no vertex of $V$. Equivalently, $\mathcal{R}$ is the Fraïssé limit of the class of finite graphs. For a finite graph $F$, write $\binom{\mathcal{R}}{F}$ for the set of induced copies of $F$ inside $\mathcal{R}$.

A coloring $c:\binom{\mathcal{R}}{F}\to\mathbb{N}$ is $k$-bounded if $|c^{-1}(n)|\le k$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$. The rainbow Ramsey theorem for the Rado graph at $F$, denoted $\mathrm{RRT}^F(\mathcal{R})$, asserts: for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $k$-bounded coloring $c$ of $\binom{\mathcal{R}}{F}$, there exists an induced subgraph $\mathcal{R}'\subseteq\mathcal{R}$ isomorphic to $\mathcal{R}$ such that $c$ restricted to $\binom{\mathcal{R}'}{F}$ is injective (a "rainbow" copy of $\mathcal{R}$).

Working in the framework of reverse mathematics over the base system $\mathrm{RCA}_0$, compare the principles $\mathrm{RRT}^F(\mathcal{R})$ as $F$ ranges over finite graphs. Specifically: 

(a) For any two finite graphs $F_1,F_2$, determine whether $\mathrm{RRT}^{F_1}(\mathcal{R})$ and $\mathrm{RRT}^{F_2}(\mathcal{R})$ are equivalent over $\mathrm{RCA}_0$, or whether one strictly implies the other.

(b) In particular, does the number of vertices $|V(F)|$ affect the reverse-mathematical strength of $\mathrm{RRT}^F(\mathcal{R})$? Are all the principles $\{\mathrm{RRT}^F(\mathcal{R}):F\text{ finite graph}\}$ pairwise equivalent over $\mathrm{RCA}_0$, or do they form a strict hierarchy depending on $|V(F)|$ (or on other structural features of $F$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a problem list on the reverse mathematics of Ramsey theory on the Rado graph. Related work (e.g., Csima–Mileti on the rainbow Ramsey theorem for $\mathbb{N}$, and rainbow Ramsey results for homogeneous structures) addresses the rainbow Ramsey theorem in other settings, but no published source found resolves the comparison of strengths of $\mathrm{RRT}^F(\mathcal{R})$ as the finite graph $F$ varies. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Strength of the Rainbow Ramsey Theorem (Csima–Mileti)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the reverse-mathematical and computability-theoretic strength of the rainbow Ramsey theorem for colorings of [N]^n, but not for the Rado graph.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational work on rainbow Ramsey strength, but does not address the Rado-graph variant parametrized by finite graphs F.

status_evidence.title: Rainbow Ramsey simple structures (Discrete Mathematics)
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that a class of homogeneous binary relational structures generalizing the Rado graph is rainbow Ramsey.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes rainbow Ramsey property for the Rado graph but does not analyze the reverse-mathematical strength as F varies.

status_evidence.title: The reverse mathematics of Ramsey-type theorems (Patey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of reverse-mathematical strengths of Ramsey-type principles; no resolution of the F-dependence of RRT for the Rado graph.
status_evidence.claim: No known reduction comparing RRT^{F_1}(R) and RRT^{F_2}(R) is recorded.
